column3: From the Old Turkic verb kör- "to see"; the word göz comes from köz, the nominal form of the same root. Derivatives such as görev, görgü and gösteri were also coined from this root during the Language Reform (1930s).
Old Turkic verb yat-; derivatives such as yatak, yatay and yatkın come from the same root. The word "yatırım" was coined in the 20th century as an economic term.
From the Old Turkic verb böl- "to separate"; bölük (a military unit), bölge and bölüm are derived from the same root.
The verb bil-, attested since the Orkhon Inscriptions; bilge, bilgi, bilim and the 1960s coinage bilgisayar come from the same root.
Old Turkic verb yaz-; yazı, yazgı (destiny, "what is written on the forehead"), yazıt and yazılım are derived from the same root.

From the Old Turkic verb okı- "to call, to summon"; its meaning evolved into reading a written text aloud. The word okul was derived from the root oku- in the 1930s, exploiting its phonetic resemblance to French école.
Old Turkic verb seb- / sev-; sevgi, sevinç and sevimli come from the same root.
Old Turkic verb kal-; kalıntı, kalıcı and kalan are derived from the same root.
Old Turkic verb al-; alım, alıcı, alıntı, alışkanlık and alışveriş come from the same root.
From the Old Turkic verb bér- (b- > v- shift); veri, verim and vergi are derived from the same root.
From the Old Turkic verb kel- (k- > g- shift); gelir, gelin, gelenek and gelecek come from the same root.
From the Old Turkic verb kit- / két-; gidiş, gider and gidermek come from the same root.
From the Old Turkic verb tur- (t- > d- shift); durum, durak and duruşma come from the same root.
Old Turkic verb tut-; tutum, tutsak, tutanak, tutku and tutkal come from the same root.
Old Turkic verb kes-; kesin, kesim, kesit and kesinti are derived from the same root.
Old Turkic verb sür-; süre, sürekli, süreç, sürgün and sürücü come from the same root.

Old Turkic verb bak-; bakım, bakış, bakan and bakanlık come from the same root. Bakan, in the sense of "one who looks after state affairs," was coined in the 1930s to replace the Arabic vekil / nazır.

column2: to count, to reckon; to show respect
column3: From the Old Turkic verb sa- / say-; sayı, sayım, saygı, sayın and sayaç come from the same root.
From the Old Turkic verb tüş-; düşünce, düşünmek (tüşün- "to fall into one's mind"), düşük and düşkün come from the same root.

column2: to be, to become, to exist
column3: From the Old Turkic verb bol- (loss of initial b-); olay, olanak, olası, oluşum and olgu are derived from the same root.
Old Turkic verb bul-; buluş, bulgu and buluntu come from the same root.
From the Old Turkic verb keç-; geçit, geçmiş, geçerli and geçim come from the same root.
Old Turkic verb aç-; açık, açıklama and açılış are derived from the same root.
From the Old Turkic verb yap- "to cover, to close, to build"; yapı, yapım, yapıt and yapay come from the same root.
Old Turkic verb çek-; çekim, çekici, çekince and çekiç are derived from the same root.
From the Old Turkic verb koş- "to add, to place side by side"; koşu, koşul (condition) and koşucu come from the same root.
Old Turkic verb sor-; soru, sorun, sorgu and sorumlu are derived from the same root.
From bağ, the nominal form of the Old Turkic verb ba- "to bind"; bağlantı, bağlam, bağımlı and bağımsız come from the same root.
From the Old Turkic verb tog- / tug-; doğu (the direction where the sun rises), doğa, doğal and doğum are derived from the same root.
Old Turkic verb bat-; batı (the direction where the sun sets), batak and batkın come from the same root.
From the Old Turkic noun yaş "year, lifetime" and the verb yaşa-; yaşam, yaşıt and yaşlı come from the same root.
Old Turkic verb uç-; uçak (a 1930s coinage), uçuş, uçurtma and uçurum come from the same root.
From the Old Turkic verb bin- / mün-; binek and binici come from the same root.
From the Old Turkic verb én- / in-; iniş and indirim come from the same root.
From the Old Turkic verb çık- / taşık-; çıkış, çıkar, çıktı and çıkıntı are derived from the same root.
From the Old Turkic verb kir-; giriş, girdi and girişim come from the same root.
Old Turkic verb taşı-; taşıt, taşıma and taşınmak come from the same root.
Old Turkic verb yé-; yem, yemiş and yiyecek come from the same root. Vowel narrowing: ye-yor > yiyor.
Old Turkic verb iç-; içki, içecek and içim come from the same root.
Old Turkic verb öl-; ölüm, ölü, öldürmek and ölümsüz come from the same root.
From the Old Turkic noun ög "mind" and the verb ögren-; öğrenci, öğretmen, öğüt and öğreti are derived from the same root.
From the Old Turkic verb ür- / üre-; ürün, üretim and üretmek come from the same root.
From the Old Turkic verbs büt- "to be completed" and bit- "to grow"; bitki, bitim and bitirmek come from the same root.

column2: to burn; to set on fire
column3: Old Turkic verb yan- and its causative yak-; yangın, yanık, yakıt and yakıcı come from the same root.
Old Turkic verb kır-; kırık, kırılgan, kırıntı and kırgın come from the same root.
Old Turkic verb sat-; satış, satıcı and satın come from the same root.
Old Turkic verb at-; atış, atılım and atık come from the same root.
From the Old Turkic verb tik-; dikiş, dikey and dikili come from the same root.
Old Turkic verb ek-; ekin, ekim and ekmek (the food: ek- + -mek) come from the same root.
From the Old Turkic noun yük; yüklemek, yüksek and yükselmek come from the same root.
Old Turkic verb bas-; baskı, basın, basamak, baskın and basınç are derived from the same root.
Old Turkic verb kap-; kapı, kapak, kapalı, kaplamak and kapsamak come from the same root.
Old Turkic verb ör-; örgü, örtü, örtmek and örgüt come from the same root.

column2: to strike; to play (an instrument); to steal
column3: From the Old Turkic verb çal- "to strike"; çalgı, çalışmak and çalışma come from the same root.
Old Turkic verb an-; anı, anıt, anlam, anlamak and anlaşma are derived from the same root.
From the Old Turkic verb tanu-; tanık, tanım and tanıtım come from the same root.

column2: to arrive, to reach; to exist
column3: From the Old Turkic verb bar- (b- > v-); varlık, varış and varsayım come from the same root.
From the Old Turkic verb té-; deyim and dedikodu come from the same root. Vowel narrowing: de-yor > diyor.
From the Old Turkic verb tön-; dönem, dönüş, dönüşüm and döngü come from the same root.
From the Old Turkic verb ula- "to join, to connect"; ulak, ulaşım and ulaştırma come from the same root.
Old Turkic verb kon-; konak, konu, konuk, konum, konut and komşu (konşı) come from the same root.

column2: to smoke, to give off smoke
column3: Old Turkic verb tüt-; tütün and tütsü come from the same root.
From the Old Turkic verbs yor- "to interpret, to explain (a dream)" and yor- "to tire"; yorgun and yorum come from the same root.
From the Old Turkic verb bog-; boğaz and boğum come from the same root.
Old Turkic verb çöz-; çözüm and çözelti come from the same root.
From the Old Turkic verb üz- "to cut, to break"; üzüntü and üzgün come from the same root.
From the Old Turkic verb tol-; dolu, dolma and dolgu come from the same root. Dolma has passed into the Balkan languages and Greek.
Old Turkic word boş; boşluk, boşanmak and boşaltmak come from the same root.
From the Old Turkic verb yorı-; yürüyüş and yürek (yüre- "to beat") are considered to come from the same root.
Old Turkic verb kork-; korku, korkunç and korkak come from the same root.
From the Old Turkic verb kül-; gülüş, gülünç and güldürü come from the same root.
From the Old Turkic verb ıgla-; ağlayış and ağıt come from the same root.
Old Turkic verb sıg-; sığınak, sığınmak and sığınmacı come from the same root.
From the Old Turkic verb yaşu- / ışı-; ışık, ışın and ışıldak come from the same root.

The Arabic triliteral root k-t-b "to write"; kitâb (a written thing), kâtib (one who writes), mektûb (what has been written) and mekteb (a place where writing is done) are different patterns of the same root.
The Arabic root ḥ-k-m; ḥakīm (sage, physician), ḥākim (one who rules), ḥukm (judgment), maḥkeme (place of judgment) and ḥikmet (wisdom) derive from the same root.
The Arabic root s-l-m; selâm (well-being), İslâm (submission), müslim (one who submits), teslîm and selâmet come from the same root.
The Arabic root ʿ-l-m; ʿilm (knowledge), ʿālim (one who knows), muʿallim (one who teaches), taʿlîm (teaching), maʿlûm (known) and ʿalem (world) derive from the same root.
The Arabic root k-l-m; kelime (word), kelâm (speech) and mükâleme (dialogue) come from the same root.
The Arabic root ʿ-q-l "to bind, to restrain"; ʿaql (intellect), ʿāqil (intelligent) and maʿqūl (reasonable) derive from the same root.
The Arabic root f-k-r; fikr (thought), tefekkür (deep reflection), mütefekkir (thinker) and efkâr (thoughts; in Turkish "worry") come from the same root.

column2: to measure, to have power over
column3: The Arabic root q-d-r; qader (one's measured lot, destiny), qudret (power), taqdîr (appraisal), miqdâr (measure) and iqtidâr (holding power) derive from the same root.
The Arabic root ḥ-s-b; ḥisâb (account, calculation) and muḥâsebe (settling of accounts) come from the same root.
The Arabic root ş-k-r; şükr, teşekkür, şükrân and müteşekkir derive from the same root.
The Arabic root r-ḥ-m; raḥmet, merḥamet, raḥîm, raḥmân and merḥûm (one who has attained mercy, the deceased) come from the same root.
The Arabic root k-w-n; mekân (place where one is), kâinât (all that exists), imkân (possibility) and mümkün derive from the same root.

column2: to stand up, to stand upright
column3: The Arabic root q-w-m; qiyâm, qiyâmet, maqâm (place where one stands), muqâvemet (resistance), qavim, istiqâmet and taqvîm come from the same root.
The Arabic root ʿ-m-l; ʿamel (deed, work), ʿamele (laborer), muʿâmele (transaction), maʿmûl (manufactured) and teʿâmül derive from the same root.
The Arabic root ş-h-d; şâhid (witness), şehîd (one who bears witness, martyr), şehâdet and müşâhede come from the same root.
The Arabic root ḥ-s-n; ḥüsn (beauty), iḥsân (benevolence), taḥsîn (approval) and muḥsin derive from the same root.

column2: to set out on a journey
column3: The Arabic root s-f-r; sefer (journey), müsâfir (traveler), sefîr (envoy), sefâret and sofra (originally a spread of travel provisions) come from the same root.
The Arabic root n-ẕ-r; naẕar (glance), manẕara (a place looked upon, view), nâẕır (one who looks, overseer), naẕariye (theory) and münâẕara derive from the same root.
The Arabic root ẕ-k-r; ẕikr (remembrance), teẕkere, müẕâkere (mutual recollection, deliberation) and meẕkûr come from the same root.
The Arabic root ḫ-b-r; ḫaber, muḫâbir, muḫâbere, iḫbâr and istiḫbârât derive from the same root.
The Arabic root ṭ-l-b; ṭaleb (request), ṭalebe (seekers, students), ṭâlib and maṭlûb come from the same root.
The Arabic root d-r-s; ders, medrese (place of lessons), müderris, tedrîs and tedrisat derive from the same root.
The Arabic root ʿ-r-f; ʿârif (one who knows), ʿirfân, maʿrifet, iʿtirâf, ʿörf (known custom), taʿrîf and maʿrûf come from the same root.
The Arabic root ḥ-r-k; ḥareket, taḥrîk, ḥarekât and müteḥarrik derive from the same root.

column2: to reach, to be united with
column3: The Arabic root w-ṣ-l; vuṣlat (union), vesîle (means, intermediary), vâṣıl and ittiṣâl come from the same root.
The Arabic root ṭ-b-ʿ; ṭabîʿat (innate nature), ṭabîʿî, maṭbaʿa (printing house) and maṭbûʿât derive from the same root.
The Arabic root ṭ-b-b; ṭıbb (medicine), ṭabîb (physician) and ṭabâbet come from the same root.
The Arabic root ʿ-d-l; ʿadâlet, ʿâdil, ʿadliye, iʿtidâl (balance), muʿâdil and taʿdîl derive from the same root.
The Arabic root ḥ-q-q; ḥaqq (truth, right), ḥaqîqat, ḥuqûq (rights), ḥaqîqî, taḥqîq and muḥaqqaq come from the same root.

column2: to cling like ivy, to love
column3: The Arabic root ʿ-ş-q; ʿaşq, ʿâşıq and maʿşûq derive from the same root.

column2: to draw, to leave a mark
column3: The Arabic root r-s-m; resm (drawing), resmî (recorded, official), merâsim (ceremonies) and ressâm come from the same root.

column2: to arrange, to put in order
column3: The Arabic root n-ẕ-m; niẕâm (order), intiẕâm, muntaẕam, nâẕım, manẕûm and tanẕîm (the Tanzimat) derive from the same root.
The Arabic root ḥ-y-y; ḥayât (life), ḥayvân (living being) and iḥyâ (revival) come from the same root.
The Arabic root m-l-k; mülk, melik (king), memleket, mülkiyet, mâlik and emlâk derive from the same root.
The Arabic root ḥ-r-r; ḥürr (free), ḥürriyet, taḥrîr (writing; liberation) and muḥarrir (writer) come from the same root.
The Arabic root ş-r-k; şirket (partnership), şerîk (partner), iştirâk, müşterek and şirk derive from the same root.
The Arabic root c-m-ʿ; câmiʿ (that which gathers), cumʿa (day of assembly), cemâʿat, cemiyet, mecmûʿa (compilation) and ictimâʿ come from the same root.
The Arabic root c-m-l; cümle (whole), cemâl (beauty) and cemîl derive from the same root.
The Arabic root q-l-b; qalb (that which turns, heart), qâlib (mold) and inqılâb (revolution) come from the same root.
The Arabic root q-w-l; qavl (saying), maqâle (what is said, article) and muqâvele (mutual word, contract) derive from the same root.
The Arabic root w-c-d; vücûd (existence, body), mevcûd, vecd, vicdân and îcâd (finding, invention) come from the same root.
The Arabic root n-q-l; naql, naqliye, naqliyât, menqûl and intiqâl derive from the same root.

column2: to appoint as deputy, to trust
column3: The Arabic root w-k-l; vekîl, vekâlet, tevekkül and müvekkil come from the same root.
The Arabic root ş-ʿ-r; şiʿr (poetry), şâʿir and şuʿûr (consciousness) derive from the same root.
The Arabic root ş-h-r; şöhret, meşhûr and teşhîr come from the same root.
The Arabic root f-ʿ-l; fiʿl (action), fâʿil (doer), faʿâl, faʿâliyet and mefʿûl derive from the same root.
The Arabic root ʿ-b-d; ʿibâdet, maʿbed (place of worship), maʿbûd (that which is worshipped) and ʿubûdiyet come from the same root.
The Arabic root k-s-r; kesr (broken part, fraction), kusûr (deficiency) and inkisâr derive from the same root.
The Arabic root ḥ-f-ẕ; ḥâfıẕ, ḥıfẕ, muḥâfaẕa, muḥâfıẕ, maḥfûẕ and ḥâfıẕa come from the same root.
The Arabic root ṣ-n-ʿ; ṣanʿat (skill in making), ṣanâyiʿ (crafts) and ṣınâʿî derive from the same root.
The Arabic root m-d-n; medeniyet, medenî and Medîne (city) come from the same root.
The Arabic root s-y-s; siyâset (horse training > governance), siyâsî and seyis (groom) derive from the same root.
The Arabic root d-w-r; devr (rotation), devre, dâire (that which turns, circle), idâre (making turn, administration), müdîr (one who makes turn, director) and devrân come from the same root.
The Arabic root ṭ-r-f; ṭaraf, eṭrâf (sides), bîṭaraf and ṭaraftâr derive from the same root.
The Arabic root w-z-n; vezn (measure, meter), mîzân (scales) and vezne come from the same root.
The Arabic root ḥ-m-l; ḥammâl, ḥâmile (one who bears a load), ḥamle, taḥammül and iḥtimâl derive from the same root.
The Arabic root ḥ-r-f; ḥarf, taḥrîf (altering letters, distortion) and ḥarfiyen come from the same root.
The Arabic root ʿ-h-d; ʿahd, taʿahhüd and muʿâhede derive from the same root.

column2: to split, to create; to break a fast
column3: The Arabic root f-ṭ-r; fıṭrat (innate nature), ifṭâr (breaking the fast) and fiṭre come from the same root.
The Arabic root s-c-d; secde, mescid (place of prostration) and seccâde derive from the same root.

column2: to be good, to set right
column3: The Arabic root ṣ-l-ḥ; ṣulḥ (peace), ıṣlâḥ, ṣâliḥ and maṣlaḥat come from the same root.
The Arabic root d-ʿ-w; duʿâ (call, prayer), daʿvâ (claim), daʿvet and iddiʿâ derive from the same root.
The Arabic root ṭ-l-ʿ; ṭâliʿ (rising star, fortune) and muṭâlaʿa (examination) come from the same root.
The Arabic root ḥ-w-l; ḥâl, aḥvâl, ḥavâle and taḥvîl derive from the same root.
The Arabic root ḫ-l-q; ḫalq (created beings, people), ḫilqat, aḫlâq (dispositions, morals) and maḫlûq come from the same root.
The Arabic root ṣ-d-q; ṣâdıq, ṣadaqa, ṣadâqat and taṣdîq derive from the same root.

column2: to be great; to be resolute
column3: The Arabic roots ʿ-ẕ-m / ʿ-z-m; ʿazm (resolve), ʿaẕamet (greatness) and muʿaẕẕam come from the same root.
The Arabic root k-m-l; kemâl, kâmil, tekâmül, mükemmel and ikmâl derive from the same root.
The Arabic root ṣ-w-r; ṣûret (form), taṣvîr and taṣavvur come from the same root.
The Arabic root n-f-s; nefes, nefis (soul, self), nüfûs (souls, population) and teneffüs derive from the same root.
The Arabic root h-d-y; hediye and hidâyet come from the same root.
The Arabic root k-f-r; kâfir, küfür and kefâret derive from the same root.
The Arabic root ṣ-b-r; ṣabr, ṣâbir and ṣabûr come from the same root.
The Arabic root ẕ-h-r; ẕâhir, ẕuhûr, teẕâhür and maẕhar derive from the same root.
The Arabic root ḥ-k-y; ḥikâye and ḥikâyet come from the same root.
The Arabic root ʿ-q-d; ʿaqd (contract), ʿaqîde (creed) and iʿtiqâd derive from the same root.
The Arabic root c-h-d; cehd, cihâd, ictihâd and mücâhid come from the same root.
The -dār derivative of the Persian verb dāştan "to hold"; hükümdar, defterdar, dindar, taraftar, hissedar, bayraktar and sancaktar are formed with the same suffix.
Persian ḫāne "house"; hastane, postane, kütüphane, eczane, pastane, dershane, kahvehane, meyhane and hapishane are formed with the same second element.
The suffix -kār from the Persian verb kerden "to do"; sanatkâr, hizmetkâr, bestekâr, günahkâr, sahtekâr and fedakâr are formed with the same suffix.
-zede from the Persian verb zeden "to strike"; afetzede, kazazede and depremzede are formed with the same suffix.
The Persian suffix -stān "place"; bostan, gülistan, Hindistan, Yunanistan, Macaristan and Türkistan are formed with the same suffix.
Persian nāme "letter, writing"; beyanname, seyahatname, nizamname, vekâletname and şahname are formed with the same second element.
-bāz from the Persian verb bāzīden "to play"; cambaz, hokkabaz, düzenbaz, kumarbaz and sihirbaz are formed with the same suffix.
Old Persian xšāyaθiya "king"; şah, padişah, şehzade, şahane and the chess term "şah mat" (checkmate) come from the same root.
Persian pā(y) "foot"; pabuç (pā-pūş: foot covering), paça, pijama (pā-cāme: leg garment, via Urdu) and payitaht come from the same root.
Persian ser "head"; serdar, serbest (literally "head-bound," now "free"), sermaye (principal capital), serüven (ser-güzeşt) and serhat come from the same root.
Persian āb "water"; abdest (hand water, ritual ablution), hoşaf (pleasant water) and gülab come from the same root.
Latin specere "to look"; spektrum (that which is seen), perspektif (looking through), prospektüs (looking ahead), spekülasyon (observation) and spesifik come from the same root.
Latin trahere / tractare "to pull"; traktör (that which pulls), kontrat (drawn up together), portre (drawn out), tren and antrenman come from the same root.
Ancient Greek gráphein "to scratch, to write"; fotoğraf, telgraf, paragraf, coğrafya, grafik, program, gramer and biyografi come from the same root.
Ancient Greek lógos "word, reason"; analog, diyalog, katalog, biyoloji, psikoloji, teknoloji and ekoloji come from the same root.
Ancient Greek tékhnē "craft"; teknik, teknoloji, teknisyen and teknokrat come from the same root.
Ancient Greek pólis "city"; politika, polis, metropol, polisiye and kozmopolit come from the same root.
Latin caput "head"; kaptan (the one at the head), kapital (principal money), kapitalizm, kapitülasyon, kep, şapka and kapüşon come from the same root.
Latin mittere "to send"; misyon, komisyon, komite, mesaj, emisyon and transmisyon come from the same root.
Latin ponere "to put"; pozisyon, pozitif, kompozisyon, depo and depozito come from the same root.
Latin facere "to make"; fabrika, fakülte, efekt, fason and ofis come from the same root.
Latin videre "to see"; video, vizyon, televizyon, vize and revizyon come from the same root.
Latin currere "to run"; kurs, koridor, kurye and konkur come from the same root.
Latin ducere "to lead"; prodüktör, prodüksiyon, kondüktör, redüksiyon, dük and düşes come from the same root.
Latin portare "to carry"; rapor, pasaport, portatif and transport come from the same root.
Latin stare "to stand" and Greek hístanai; istasyon, statü, istatistik, enstitü, sistem and asistan come from the same Indo-European root.
Ancient Greek phōnḕ "sound"; telefon, mikrofon, fonetik, senfoni and megafon come from the same root.
Ancient Greek kýklos "circle"; bisiklet, siklon, ansiklopedi, sirk and sirkülasyon come from the same root.
Ancient Greek krátos "power"; demokrasi, bürokrasi, aristokrasi, otokrasi and teknokrat come from the same root.
Ancient Greek dḕmos "people"; demokrasi, demografi, epidemi and pandemi come from the same root.
Ancient Greek phaínein "to show, to shine"; fener, fanus, fantezi, fenomen, fantastik and fantom come from the same root.
Ancient Greek pân "all"; panayır (pan-ēgyris: general assembly), pandemi, panorama, panteon and pankreas come from the same root.
Ancient Greek métron "measure"; metre, termometre, kilometre, geometri, simetri, parametre and barometre come from the same root.
Ancient Greek hodós "way"; metot (a going along a way), periyot (a circular way), katot, anot and elektrot come from the same root.

The word baş "head, summit; leader" in the Orkhon Inscriptions; Ottoman rank and office titles such as onbaşı, yüzbaşı, binbaşı, başçavuş, başbuğ, bölükbaşı, odabaşı, kapıcıbaşı, bostancıbaşı and topçubaşı, as well as kızılbaş, come from the same root.

The word beg "lord" in the Orkhon Inscriptions; beylik, beylerbeyi, sancakbeyi, uçbeyi, derebeyi, begüm and atabey, along with albay and yarbay, which the Language Reform (1930s) formed from the word bay, derive from the same root.
Old Turkic tuğ "a horsetail standard as an emblem of sovereignty"; tuğcu, tugay (a unit entitled to a standard), tuğgeneral and tuğamiral come from the same root.
tüm, related to Old Turkic tümen "ten thousand"; tümgeneral, tümamiral and tümbay (commander of a division) were derived from the same root.
kor, formed during the Language Reform (1930s) by shortening the word kolordu; korgeneral, koramiral and korbay were derived from the same abbreviation.

The word ordu "the ruler's encampment" in the Orkhon Inscriptions; orda (the Golden Horde), ordubozan, orgeneral and oramiral come from the same root; horde in the European languages also spread from here.
Old Turkic teg- "to touch, to reach"; the Language Reform (1930s) coinages teğmen (one who corresponds), üsteğmen, asteğmen and teğmenlik were derived from this root.
The word sü "army" in the Orkhon Inscriptions; subaşı (sü başı: army commander), sübaşılık, astsubay and the Language Reform (1930s) coinage subay come from the same root.
The word er "man, brave warrior" in the Orkhon Inscriptions; erlik, erat, erbaş, eren and erkeklik derive from the same root.
Old Turkic kol "arm, side"; kolordu, kolağası, kolcu, kolluk, kolaçan and kolbaşı were derived from the same root in military language.
Old Turkic yet- "to lead (an animal) by a halter"; yedmek, yedek (a horse led alongside, a spare) and yedeklemek come from the same root.
Old Turkic ata- "to give a name"; atamak and atama (appointment to office) derive from the same root.
Mongolian cebe "armor, weapon"; cebeci (armorer) and cebelü (armored soldier) come from the same root; cebehane and cephane were formed with Persian ḫāne.
Old Turkic sol "left side"; solak (left-handed person; a sultan's guard) and solcu derive from the same root.
The word kul "slave" in the Orkhon Inscriptions; kulluk (servitude; a guard post) and kapıkulu (slave of the palace gate) come from the same root.
Old Turkic aka/ağa "elder brother, chief"; ağalık, ağabey, yeniçeriağası, haremağası, kızlarağası, kapıağası, akağa and karaağa derive from the same root.
Old Turkic tér- "to gather"; dermek, devşirmek (dévşür-), devşirme and derleme come from the same root.
Old Turkic yama- "to repair by adding"; yamak (assistant) and yamalı derive from the same root.
The word tirig "alive" in the Orkhon Inscriptions; diri, dirilmek and dirlik (livelihood; a timar's revenue) come from the same root.
Mongolian casa- "to regulate"; yasa, yasak, along with yasavul (officer of order), yasakçı and yasaklamak, derive from the same root.
The verb buyur- "to command" in the Orkhon Inscriptions; buyruk (command; high official) and buyruldu (a vizier's decree) come from the same root.
Old Turkic and Mongolian baġatur "brave warrior"; batur and bahadır, which came via Persian, are from the same root; Russian bogatır and Hungarian bátor also spread from here.
The word alp "brave warrior, hero" in the Orkhon Inscriptions; alplık, alpagut (a warrior who attacks alone) and alperen derive from the same root.
The word ok in the Orkhon Inscriptions; okçu, okluk and okçuluk come from the same root.
Old Turkic art "back, ridge"; artçı (rearguard unit) and ardıl are derived from the same root.
Old Turkic yaġma "plunder"; yağmacı and yağmalamak come from the same root; Persian yaġmā was also borrowed from Turkish.
Old Turkic çap- "to strike; to gallop a horse"; çapmak, çapul (raid), çapulcu, çapar (courier) and çapkın derive from the same root.
Old Turkic bus- "to lie in ambush"; pusmak, pusu (busuġ) and pusucu come from the same root.

Old Turkic buz- "to destroy, to scatter"; bozmak, bozuk, bozulmak, bozgun and bozguncu come from the same root.

The Arabic root w-ẓ-f; vazife, muvazzaf and tevzif come from the same root.

column3: The Arabic root ḍ-b-ṭ; zapt, zaptetmek, zabit, zabıta, zaptiye, zabıt, mazbata and inzibat come from the same root.
The Arabic root ẓ-f-r; zafer, muzaffer, zafername and zaferyab derive from the same root.
The Arabic root ġ-l-b; galip, galibiyet, galebe, tagallüp, mağlup and mağlubiyet come from the same root.
The Arabic root ġ-n-m; ganimet and iğtinam derive from the same root.
The Arabic root ġ-r-b; garip, gurbet and gureba (strangers; a cavalry regiment) come from the same root.
The Arabic root ş-q-w; şaki, eşkıya and şekavet derive from the same root.
The Arabic root ş-r-f; şeref, şerif, eşraf, teşrif, teşrifat and müşerref come from the same root.

Persian ḫunb "jar"; humbara (little jar: hand grenade), kumbara and humbaracı come from the same root.

Persian āsūdan "to rest"; asayiş (tranquility, public order) and asude come from the same root.

Latin manus "hand"; manevra (handwork), manüel and manifesto come from the same root.
Latin imperare "to command"; imparator, imparatorluk, emperyalizm and emperyalist derive from the same root.

Latin caballus "horse"; şövalye (horseman, knight) and kavalye come from the same root.
Latin senior "older"; senyör and senatör derive from the same root.
Medieval Latin feudum "fief"; feodal, feodalizm and feodalite come from the same root.
Latin miles "soldier"; milis, militan, militarizm and militarist derive from the same root.
Latin terrere "to frighten"; terör, terörist and terörizm come from the same root.
French sabot "wooden clog"; sabotaj (wrecking machinery with a clog) and sabotör derive from the same root.
